ogDesc: Explore Buriram across Khmer heritage and sports culture — Phanom Rung, Mueang Tam, Khao Kradong, Chang Arena, Wat Khao Phra Angkhan. Admission fees, opening hours, and trip planning included.
eyebrow: See Buriram Like a Local · Updated 2026
intro: Buriram lets you mix ancient Khmer civilization and sports culture in a single trip. Drive up to Phanom Rung on a dormant volcano crater in the morning, drop by Prasat Mueang Tam in the afternoon, and cheer on the football team at Chang Arena in the evening. Here are the 10 attractions visitors to Buriram should not miss — Khmer stone sanctuaries, a volcano, a hilltop temple, and the landmarks of a proud sports city.

blocks.html:
When people think of Buriram, football and motor racing often come to mind first — but the province's real charm is the way ancient Khmer civilization and a modern sports city sit side by side. Drive south from town toward Chaloem Phra Kiat and Prakhon Chai and you reach pink sandstone towers standing tall on the rim of an extinct volcano. Back in town, Khao Kradong Forest Park invites a walk up to pay respects and take in the view, Saoh Krao Walking Street fills up in the evenings, and Chang Arena sits next to one of Asia's premier racing circuits. Whatever your travel style, easy-going Lower Isan does not disappoint.

The star of the show is Phanom Rung, one of the most beautiful pieces of Khmer art in Thailand — and home to the famous solar alignment when the rising or setting sun shines through all 15 doorways, four times a year, drawing huge crowds every time. Nearby Prasat Mueang Tam can be visited on the same trip with a combined ticket. Chang Arena seats over 32,600 and Chang International Circuit is an FIA Grade 1 venue that hosts the season-opening round of MotoGP each February. Plan a loop that covers both the heritage trail and the sports scene and you will understand why Buriram keeps pulling people back.

blocks.name: Phanom Rung Historical Park (Prasat Hin Phanom Rung)
blocks.signature: Pink sandstone Khmer sanctuary on an extinct volcano crater, with an annual solar alignment through 15 doorways twice a year, and a dramatic long causeway approach
blocks.descHtml:
Coming to Buriram and skipping Phanom Rung is like not really arriving. This is an ancient Khmer sandstone sanctuary perched on the summit of Phanom Rung — the crater of a long-extinct volcano. The stones are a warm pink-orange that glows especially beautifully in early morning or late afternoon light, and the site rewards history enthusiasts, architecture lovers, and photographers equally. Families and older visitors can walk through comfortably as long as they pace themselves on the uphill approach.

The standout feature that every visitor mentions is the long ceremonial walkway to the sanctuary: you pass the Nang Riang pillars, cross the Naga Bridge, and climb the stairway to the main prang. Looking back along the approach gives you a sweeping panoramic view. Inside, do not miss the Narai Bantom Sin lintel — the celebrated piece that was once the subject of an international repatriation effort. And the solar alignment itself, when sunrise or sunset lines up perfectly through all 15 doorways, draws enormous crowds four times a year: sunrise around early April and early September, sunset around early March and early October. If you come on those days, secure your viewing spot before dawn.

Admission is excellent value: 20 THB for Thais, 100 THB for foreigners, and free for visitors aged 60 and over. There is parking at Gate 1 (free) and at the upper lot (small fee). The site opens daily roughly 06:00–18:00. It sits in Tambon Ta Pek, Chaloem Phra Kiat District, about 60 km south of Buriram town — an easy drive, and most visitors combine it with Prasat Mueang Tam nearby.

Reviewers consistently warn that the summit is exposed and sunny with very little shade, so bring a hat, umbrella, water, and comfortable shoes. If you are not coming for the solar alignment, early morning or late afternoon is far more pleasant than midday. With a Google rating of 4.7 from tens of thousands of reviews, it is easy to see why this is one of the top destinations in Lower Isan.
mustOrder: The long sandstone causeway, Naga Bridge, and stairway to the main prang
Narai Bantom Sin lintel at the main prang
Solar alignment through all 15 doorways (4 times a year)
Panoramic view from the extinct volcano crater
blocks.bestFor: History and photography lovers — come in the morning or late afternoon to avoid the sun

blocks.name: Khao Kradong Forest Park (Phra Suphat Bopit)
blocks.signature: Extinct volcano summit at 265 m, the revered city-guardian Buddha Phra Suphat Bopit, 297-step Naga stairway, a suspension bridge over the volcano crater, and panoramic views reaching Chang Arena
blocks.descHtml:
Khao Kradong Forest Park sits on a dormant volcano estimated to be 300,000–900,000 years old, rising about 265 metres above sea level — just 6 km from Buriram town centre. That proximity makes it the go-to spot for a morning worship, a view, and a walk in nature. The star is Phra Suphat Bopit, the large city-guardian Buddha at the summit, facing north. Most visitors come up to pay their respects first, whether they are families bringing elders for merit-making or fitness enthusiasts tackling the stairway.

There are several highlights not to miss. Start with the 297-step Naga staircase that winds up to the Buddha — those who prefer not to climb can drive up and park at the top. Next is the suspension bridge spanning the volcano crater, roughly 59 metres long and more than ten metres above the ground. The lava and basalt formations below are the real thing. From the viewpoint at the summit you can see Buriram city, the reservoir, and all the way to Chang Arena. Multiple reviews agree: the view is worth the climb, especially at sunset.

Best of all, it is completely free. Budget a bit for fuel, merit-making donations, and snacks from the stalls at the entrance. The park opens daily around 08:00–18:00. Mornings and late afternoons are ideal — midday heat on the exposed steps can be tough. The upper car park has limited spaces, so on public holidays and festivals you may need to wait. Arriving early gives you a much smoother visit.

Khao Kradong ranks highly among Buriram's attractions because it packs sacred history, a rare dormant volcano, and a fine city panorama into one to two hours of easy walking. It makes a natural first stop in Buriram before heading to Chang Arena in the evening.
mustOrder: Pay respects to Phra Suphat Bopit, the city-guardian Buddha
Walk the suspension bridge over the volcano crater
Climb the 297-step Naga stairway
City viewpoint with a panorama reaching Chang Arena
blocks.bestFor: Morning worship and city views — come early or at sunset

blocks.name: Chang Arena (Chang Arena Buriram)
blocks.signature: Home stadium of Buriram United — Thailand's largest club — seating 32,600 with no running track so every seat feels close to the pitch, plus a club megastore, café zone, and stadium tours
blocks.priceRange: Walking around outside free · Stadium tour ~100 THB
blocks.descHtml:
Chang Arena is the home ground of Buriram United, the football club with the largest support base in Thailand. It holds 32,600 spectators in a dedicated football stadium — no athletics track to push fans away from the pitch, just stadium-style seating like you see in Europe. The ground even entered the Guinness World Records as the fastest-built FIFA-standard stadium, completed in just 256 days. It draws both dedicated football fans wanting to feel the atmosphere of Prasat Sai Fah (the club's nickname) and casual visitors who simply want to photograph one of Buriram's most iconic landmarks.

Must-do moments include walking the outer perimeter to photograph the huge Chang ARENA sign and the elephant statues at the front, then browsing the Buriram United Mega Store for match jerseys, souvenirs, and club memorabilia at accessible prices. There is a café zone inside for a sit-down break. Stadium Tours take you behind the scenes to the player changing rooms, press conference room, and pitch-side photo spots. Most visitor reviews agree: the stadium is beautiful, clean, and larger than expected, with very convenient parking.

Wandering the outside areas and entering the shops is free. The indoor stadium tour costs around 100 THB per person and runs daily approximately 09:00–17:00, except on match days when timings change. The stadium is in Tambon Isan, Mueang Buriram — a short drive from the city centre, easy to reach by car or hired vehicle.

This is a landmark that matters whether you follow football or not. On match days the buzz of a capacity crowd is something else entirely. If you want the full atmosphere, come on a home match day — for a relaxed look around and photos, a weekday without a game works better. Check tour times with staff before visiting.
mustOrder: Photo with the Chang ARENA sign and elephant statues at the entrance
Buriram United Mega Store — jerseys and souvenirs
Stadium Tour — changing rooms, press room, pitch-side
Watch a Buriram United home match and soak up the atmosphere
blocks.bestFor: Football fans and landmark photo seekers — especially on a home match day
blocks.hours: Indoor zone ~09:00–17:00 daily (adjusted on match days)

blocks.name: Prasat Mueang Tam
blocks.signature: A Hindu Khmer sanctuary over 1,000 years old with five brick prangs, a gallery walkway, and four L-shaped reservoirs with Naga-carved stone rims — usually visited together with Phanom Rung
blocks.priceRange: 20 THB (foreigners 100 THB) · Combined ticket with Phanom Rung 30 THB / 150 THB
blocks.descHtml:
Prasat Mueang Tam is a Hindu Khmer sanctuary over a thousand years old (roughly 16th Buddhist century, Khleang-to-Baphuon style), situated in Ban Khok Mueang, Tambon Chora Khe Maak, Prakhon Chai District — only about 8 km southeast of Phanom Rung. It is ideal for anyone who wants to explore Khmer architecture without the climb, and for visitors travelling with older family members who prefer level ground. Most people pair it with Phanom Rung in a single day as both sites are along the same road.

The unmissable highlight is the cluster of five brick prangs on a single shared platform — three in front, two at the back. Unusually, there is no tall central prang elevated above the rest as in most Khmer complexes. The other feature that draws the most comments is the four L-shaped reservoirs surrounding the gallery, perfectly symmetrical, their rims carved with Naga bodies and five-headed Naga corners. Walking the sandstone gallery and examining the Kala (Kirtimukha) face lintels above each door is thoroughly rewarding. Visitor reviews consistently note that the sanctuary is well-preserved and carefully maintained.

The atmosphere here is quiet and unhurried — far fewer crowds than Phanom Rung, which makes photography easy and unhurried. There is a car park just off the entrance road. Admission: 20 THB for Thais, 100 THB for foreigners, or buy the combined ticket covering both Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam (30 THB / 150 THB) for better value. Open daily around 06:00–18:00.

This sanctuary became especially famous after it appeared as a filming location in the drama Phrom Likhit, drawing fans retracing the story. The best time to visit is early morning or late afternoon when the sun is lower, as the grounds are exposed with limited shade. Bring a hat and water, and consider stopping at the Ban Khok Mueang community nearby for local food and souvenirs.
mustOrder: Five brick prangs on a single shared platform — three front, two back
Four L-shaped reservoirs with five-headed Naga corner carvings
Sandstone gallery and doorway arches (gopura)
Kala (Kirtimukha) face lintels above the entrances
blocks.bestFor: Pair with Phanom Rung in a single trip — history and photography in the morning or late afternoon

blocks.name: Play La Ploen Flower Park
blocks.signature: A 400-rai flower park divided into roughly 6 zones — seasonal flower fields, a cactus garden, cafés, a water park, and a resort — perfect for a full day of walking and photography
blocks.descHtml:
When people in Buriram talk about somewhere you can "walk around and photograph all day," Play La Ploen is almost always the first name they mention. It is the first flower park in Lower Isan — over 400 rai in Khu Mueang District, about 30 km from Buriram town. Perfect for photography enthusiasts, couples, and families with children who can run free across the multiple zones. Most reviews say you need a comfortable two to four hours to really take it all in.

The centrepiece is six greenhouse pavilions, each with a different theme: from a cold-climate tulip and lavender house to an ancient fern forest, and a cactus zone paired with an Egyptian pyramid backdrop that many visitors love photographing. Outside, the open-air flower fields rotate with the seasons — cosmos and sunflowers are popular choices. Two other highlights are the Laedao Café (space theme) and a small children's splash area. Guests staying at the on-site resort enter the flower park free of charge.

Admission to the flower park zone runs around 150 THB for adults and 80 THB for children. Open daily 08:00–17:00. Real visitor reviews consistently describe the park as "well-arranged and photogenic," with a pleasantly calm and shaded atmosphere. Google scores sit around 4.2 stars, which is solid for an out-of-town garden.

A few things worth knowing: greenhouse flowers rotate by season, and late rainy-season to early winter (roughly November–February) usually brings the best cold-climate blooms. Check the Facebook page before visiting to see which zones are open, as occasional renovation work or events can close parts temporarily. Pack sunscreen and water for the outdoor sections — but overall this is a worthwhile stop if you are passing through Khu Mueang.
mustOrder: All 6 greenhouse pavilions — especially the tulip and lavender house
Open-air seasonal flower fields (cosmos / sunflowers)
Cactus zone and Egyptian pyramid backdrop
Laedao space-theme café + children's splash area
blocks.bestFor: Café and flower photography lovers — great for families

blocks.title: 🛏️ Buriram Accommodation — Choose a Location That Makes Sightseeing Easy
blocks.text: Getting around Buriram requires a fair bit of driving between districts. Staying in the city centre keeps things most convenient — close to Saoh Krao Walking Street, Robinson Lifestyle, and a quick ride to Chang Arena. If you are coming for football or MotoGP, a hotel near the stadium saves a lot of travel time. Compare rates across multiple sites before booking, especially during big match weekends or racing events when rooms sell out fast.

blocks.name: Saoh Krao Walking Street
blocks.signature: Buriram's first walking street — open Sat–Sun evenings with over 300 stalls of local food, crafts, souvenirs, live music, and an illuminated fountain
blocks.descHtml:
If you are in Buriram on a weekend and wondering where to spend the evening, Saoh Krao Walking Street is the first place locals will point you to. It is the province's original walking street, open since 2014. The name Saoh Krao comes from the Buriram United supporter group's chant — so the place carries real local identity. Perfect for anyone wanting a relaxed evening stroll, good food, a look at the city's atmosphere, and souvenir shopping all in one stretch. The street runs along Romburee Road in the city centre, near Klonglalom Canal, and you can walk the full length at a leisurely pace.

The centrepiece is the 300-plus stalls lining both sides — Isan home-cooked food, snacks, Thai sweets, alongside handicrafts, Buriram silk, and locally made gifts from surrounding communities. The riverside plaza is a particular favourite: a choreographed illuminated fountain dances to music while a live stage runs throughout the evening, including a kantrum folk band. Visitor reviews consistently mention that the food selection is vast and good value, with moo ping (grilled pork) and grilled meat stalls getting the most praise.

Entry is completely free. You pay only for whatever you eat and buy. Those who want to sit riverside have small tables available for around 20 THB each — eat, drink, and listen to live music. Opens Saturdays and Sundays from about 16:00–22:00 (the busiest period starts around 17:00). Centrally located, walking distance from many hotels in town, with nearby parking.

One useful note: the market relocated once before its current spot on Romburee–Khu Mueang Road near Klonglalom Canal. If an older Google Maps pin shows a different address, just ask a local — everyone in Buriram knows where it is. The street is alcohol-and-tobacco-free, so the atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming for families and groups alike. If you like evening markets with food, crafts, and live music all on one street, this delivers.
mustOrder: Isan home-cooked food + moo ping / grilled meat
Sit riverside at Klonglalom Canal — illuminated fountain and live music / kantrum band
Buriram silk + OTOP handicrafts and souvenirs
blocks.bestFor: Saturday–Sunday evenings — a laid-back stroll for food, shopping, and live music

blocks.name: Robinson Lifestyle Buriram
blocks.signature: The province's main mall — fashion brands, restaurants, a cinema, and a supermarket. Seasonal photo installations and a central air-conditioned meeting point for the whole city
blocks.descHtml:
Robinson Lifestyle Buriram is the main shopping centre of the province, situated on the Buriram–Nang Rong road on the western side of town. It is the air-conditioned meeting spot locals use almost every day. Visitors who want somewhere to walk around in the cool, grab a meal, catch a film, and pick up groceries under one roof will find everything here. Works well for families, couples, groups of friends, and anyone looking for a comfortable break from the heat.

The most frequently mentioned highlight is the restaurant zone, which brings together major brands — MK, Bar B Q Plaza, Laem Charoen Seafood, Hachibanramen, Yayoi, Swensen's, Dairy Queen, and Auntie Anne's hot pretzels (reviewers say you can smell them from halfway across the floor). The upper level has an SF Cinema. For shopping and groceries, there is a Tops supermarket and sports and fashion zones. Seasonal decorations and photo installations rotate throughout the year.

Inside it is spacious, open, and easy to walk around. Multiple reviewers praise the Starbucks outpost — good for individual or group seating, pleasant light, and a calm volume level. The Robin Food event at the activity plaza draws food stalls (Thai, Korean, Japanese, seafood) at fair prices with seating and live music. Entry is free. Per-person spending is flexible: coffee starts under 100 THB, a full meal at most restaurants runs 100–250 THB depending on the spot.

Located at 125 Moo 6, Buriram–Nang Rong Road, Tambon Isan, Mueang Buriram. Open daily 10:00–21:00, under ten minutes by car from the city centre, with spacious parking. On weekend evenings and during events, popular hot-pot restaurants may have queues — building in a bit of extra time helps.
mustOrder: SF Cinema on the upper floor
Brand-name restaurant zone (MK, Bar B Q Plaza, Laem Charoen)
Tops supermarket for groceries and food gifts
Robin Food event — affordable street food stalls
blocks.bestFor: Evening dinner and a film — family-friendly cool-down

blocks.name: Wat Khao Phra Angkhan
blocks.signature: A temple on an extinct volcano summit at around 320 m — with a distinctive multi-tiered-roof ordination hall, ancient Dvaravati boundary stones, and sweeping elevated views
blocks.descHtml:
Wat Khao Phra Angkhan sits on the summit of an extinct volcano, roughly 320 metres high, in Chaloem Phra Kiat District — less than 20 km from Phanom Rung. That proximity makes it an easy add-on for any heritage-focused day trip. Drive up and park near the top, then walk a short distance to the temple compound. For those who like a site that delivers both ancient artefacts and a broad view, this ticks both boxes. Google reviews award it 4.5 stars from over a thousand ratings, reflecting the genuine impression it leaves on most visitors.

The unmissable highlight is the ordination hall — a distinctive building with multiple tiered rooflines showing Khmer-influenced Buddhist architecture that looks unlike any ordinary temple. The outer perimeter features 108 Maravija Buddha images arranged in a circle. Inside, Buddhist mural paintings illustrate Jataka stories with English-language captions, so international visitors can follow along. Equally prized are the Dvaravati-era sandstone boundary markers (sema) dating back around 1,300 years, carved with stupas, lotus flowers, and dhamma wheels — genuine antiquities that are rarely encountered. Then there is a large reclining Buddha roughly 29 metres long in the forecourt.

The atmosphere up here is noticeably quieter than the more visited temples, especially on weekdays. Walk at a leisurely pace, pay your respects, take in the old stonework, and then head to the viewpoint for a wide-angle look over the green plains below. Free entry, no admission fee, with convenient parking. Open daily around 08:00–17:00.

Practical notes: the summit is exposed and hot, so come in the morning or late afternoon. There are no food stalls or drink vendors inside the temple compound — bring water. You will need your own vehicle, as no public transport runs directly here. Dress modestly as required in a working temple.
mustOrder: Multi-tiered-roof ordination hall + 108 Maravija Buddha images surrounding it
Dvaravati-era sandstone sema stones, approximately 1,300 years old
Large reclining Buddha, roughly 29 metres long
Elevated viewpoint over the Buriram plains
blocks.bestFor: Heritage and culture day — pair with Phanom Rung, morning or late afternoon

blocks.name: Chang International Circuit
blocks.signature: An internationally rated circuit, FIA Grade 1 and FIM Grade A, hosting MotoGP and major racing events late in the year — with track days, go-karts, and year-round driving experiences
blocks.priceRange: Group visits by prior arrangement / MotoGP tickets from a few hundred THB
blocks.descHtml:
When people think of Buriram, football and racing are often the first things that come to mind — and Chang International Circuit is the real destination for motorsport enthusiasts. Thailand's first FIA Grade 1 and FIM Grade A facility, opened in 2014, it stretches 4.554 km over 12 corners and accommodates around 50,000 spectators. It draws genuine motor racing fans, families wanting a photo with the iconic red "Destination of Speed" signage at the entrance — now a beloved check-in spot — and anyone curious about what an MotoGP-grade venue actually feels like up close.

The headline event is the late-year MotoGP round, when the whole province buzzes. Hotels sell out months ahead. Visitor reviews from race weekends praise the well-organised logistics, ample parking, efficient shuttle service within the venue, covered grandstands, food trucks, and an Expo zone for exploring between sessions. Outside race events the circuit runs activities year-round: Track Days where you can bring your own car and drive the actual circuit, Drag Racing, a Drift circuit, and Experience Drive sessions where sports and supercars are available for a hot lap or a co-pilot ride with a professional driver.

Costs depend entirely on what you come to do. MotoGP tickets range from General Admission standing areas to grandstand seats and full VIP lounges — book online well in advance as the best positions sell out quickly. For non-event visits, groups can arrange access directly with the circuit. The location is in Mueang Buriram District, right next to Chang Arena. Easy to get to, with plenty of hotels nearby.

If you are coming for MotoGP, plan your travel and accommodation well in advance — it is genuinely busy. Toilet queues at peak moments have come up in a handful of reviews, though the overall feedback on Buriram's hospitality and event management is overwhelmingly positive. For speed lovers or anyone who wants to experience an international-standard event in Thailand, this is one of the best venues in the region.
mustOrder: Photo with the "Destination of Speed" sign
Watch MotoGP late in the year
Track Day / Experience Drive activities
Hot lap with a professional driver
blocks.bestFor: Motorsport fans — especially during the late-year MotoGP round
blocks.hours: Group visits by prior arrangement / events follow the race calendar

blocks.name: Buriram Railway Station
blocks.signature: A historic central railway station decorated with Khmer-ruin and football motifs — surrounded by a food market. Famous for its 5-minute platform market and the city's gateway for train travellers.
blocks.descHtml:
Buriram Railway Station has been a fixture in the city centre since 1925, and today it is much more than a place to board a train. It is both the gateway into the city for rail travellers and a local landmark that residents are proud of. The station building is clean and well-kept, with photography corners and a definite air of the Prasat Sai Fah "Lightning Castle" sports culture all around it. If you are arriving in Buriram by train, this is your introduction to the city — and a good reason to linger a little before heading on.

The highlight that put this station on social media is the famous "5-minute platform market" — the only market of its kind on a railway platform in Thailand. Elderly vendors from Lam Plai Mat District and nearby provinces board the train with shoulder-pole baskets carrying garden vegetables, foraged greens, and ready-made home-cooked food. When the train pulls in around 08:00, everyone sells at speed in just a few minutes before collecting their goods and continuing into town. Real visitor reviews agree: if you want to see this, arrive before 08:15 or you will miss it. Another local staple is the row of grilled fishball vendors at the station entrance — buy a skewer to eat on the spot or pack some to go.

Everything here is extremely affordable. There is no entrance fee for the station or the market, and street food starts from 10 THB a piece. Some vegetable bundles at the market begin at just 10 THB. Located on Niwat Road in the city centre, you can walk easily to the clock tower area and old town. Surrounded by early-morning cafés and pla thong ko (Chinese doughnuts) vendors. The station is open 24 hours with parking available — suitable both for visitors arriving without a car and for those who want to explore the area on foot.

What makes this popular is the combination of old-school railway architecture, a market tradition that exists nowhere else in Thailand, and affordable local food all in one small area. If you are coming specifically for the 5-minute market, check the train timetable and arrive early. During big football matches or festivals it will be especially busy — build in extra time and plan for parking.
mustOrder: 5-minute platform market (arrive before 08:00)
Grilled fishballs from vendors at the station entrance
Photo spot at the historic station building
Explore the clock tower and old town neighbourhood around the station
blocks.bestFor: First morning in the province — great for train arrivals

Without a private car, booking a guided tour or transfer service for the Phanom Rung–Mueang Tam route through Klook or GetYourGuide lets you cover all the key sites in a single day without planning logistics yourself. Sports fans can also book stadium access and race event tickets in advance to avoid queuing at the venue. Ideal for visitors who want a relaxed, well-organised trip.

blocks.title: Good to Know Before Visiting Buriram

items.title: Renting a Car is Worth It
items.text: The main attractions are spread across several districts — Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam are a fair distance from town. A rental car or private driver is much more flexible than public transport. Within the city centre, Grab is available but cars can be scarce at times.

items.title: Keep Cash on Hand
items.text: Admission fees at the temples, food stalls along Saoh Krao Walking Street, and street vendors near the railway station mostly accept cash only. ATMs are available in town but hard to find near rural attractions. Bring small bills.

items.title: Get to the Temples Early
items.text: Phanom Rung and Wat Khao Phra Angkhan are elevated and exposed — arriving in the morning (opens around 07:00) means cooler conditions and smaller crowds. During the solar alignment event, arrive well before sunrise to secure a good spot.

items.title: Check the Match and Race Calendar
items.text: If you want to watch Buriram United or catch MotoGP, check the schedule and book tickets well in advance. On home match days, Chang Arena closes for stadium tours, and hotels in town sell out quickly.

items.title: Limited English Outside Major Sites
items.text: The main heritage sites have English-language signage, but at markets and local shops Thai is the primary language. Saving attraction names in Thai on your maps app and keeping a translation app handy makes a big difference.

items.title: Dress Modestly at Temples
items.text: Wat Khao Phra Angkhan and the Phra Suphat Bopit area at Khao Kradong are sacred sites. Dress respectfully — covered shoulders and knees — and remove footwear before entering the ordination hall zone as indicated by signs.

blocks.title: How to Get the Most Out of Buriram in a Single Trip
blocks.html:
Two days works best. Day one — the heritage trail: head out early to Phanom Rung Historical Park before the sun gets strong (opens from 07:00–18:00), then continue to Prasat Mueang Tam about 8 km away. Buy the combined two-temple ticket — 30 THB for Thais, 150 THB for foreigners — better value than buying separately. On the way, stop at Wat Khao Phra Angkhan on its dormant volcano summit for the elevated view.

Day two — around town: start the morning at Khao Kradong Forest Park — pay respects to Phra Suphat Bopit and walk the suspension bridge over the crater. In the afternoon, swing by Chang Arena and the Buriram United Mega Store. If you are there on a Saturday or Sunday, end the day at Saoh Krao Walking Street from 16:00–22:00 for local food and live music. Flower garden enthusiasts should add half a day at Play La Ploen in Khu Mueang District.

blocks.text: Getting around Buriram involves a fair amount of driving. Book accommodation in the city centre or near Chang Arena as a base — convenient for both the heritage trail and the sports venues. Check availability and prices in advance.

faq.q: What is the top attraction in Buriram that no one should miss?
faq.a: Phanom Rung Historical Park is the one attraction everyone associates with Buriram — a pink sandstone Khmer sanctuary on an extinct volcano crater. Close behind it are Prasat Mueang Tam (easily combined in the same day trip), Khao Kradong Forest Park in town, and Chang Arena for football fans. Temple enthusiasts should add Wat Khao Phra Angkhan to the list.

faq.q: What are the highlights of Buriram?
faq.a: The standout highlight is the solar alignment through all 15 doorways at Phanom Rung, which happens four times a year (two sunrises, two sunsets). In 2026, the sunrise alignment falls around 3–5 April. On the sports side: Chang Arena seats 32,600 and Chang International Circuit is an FIA Grade 1 venue hosting the MotoGP season-opener each February.

faq.q: How much does it cost to enter the attractions in Buriram?
faq.a: Phanom Rung: Thais 20 THB, foreigners 100 THB (age 60+ free). Prasat Mueang Tam: same rates, or buy the combined two-temple ticket at 30 THB / 150 THB. Play La Ploen: adults 150 THB, children 80 THB. Chang Arena stadium tour: around 100 THB with a guide. Khao Kradong Forest Park, Wat Khao Phra Angkhan, and Saoh Krao Walking Street are all free to enter.

faq.q: How do you get around and park in Buriram?
faq.a: The main attractions are spread across several districts — Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam are in the Chaloem Phra Kiat–Prakhon Chai area, a significant drive from town. A rental car or private vehicle works best. Each major site has its own car park. Within the city centre, Grab and motorbike taxis are available. Train arrivals at Buriram Railway Station can walk to the city-centre sights and take a car to Chang Arena.

faq.q: What are the opening hours for Buriram's attractions?
faq.a: Phanom Rung and Wat Khao Phra Angkhan open around 07:00–18:00. Prasat Mueang Tam opens 06:00–18:00. Khao Kradong Forest Park and Play La Ploen open around 08:00–17:00/18:00. Chang Arena stadium tours run in sessions around 09:30–16:00 (with a midday break). Saoh Krao Walking Street is Saturday–Sunday only, 16:00–22:00.
